one_sentence_goal: Determine whether cross-round temporal signals (deviation-trace stability and inter-client correlation) can distinguish colluding Sybils from a legitimate non-IID majority, which no single-round aggregation rule can do.
last_session_summary: Two things. (1) Unblocked task r2 and answered it. The blocker was never the experiment: run_fairness_experiment.rs called build_aggregator directly so no dss_ name resolved, and it was single-round so DSS's gate could not fire at all (stability returns 1.0 below two trace entries) — a dss_ row would have printed FedAvg's numbers and looked like a measurement. Both fixed; Experiment 2.11 (6,720 rows, 20 seeds, 20 rounds, zero attackers) shows dropping the stability conjunct does NOT reopen Claim 2: collusion-only DSS sits at 1.030 +/- 0.177 minority/majority influence, a CI containing parity, while krum (0.636) and flanders_krum (0.746) both down-weight the shifted minority. (2) Started r8, the real-model validation of section 5.14, and hit a structural limit worth recording.
phase: post-validation; hypothesis partially supported, three open design questions

hypothesis_status.claim_2_non_iid_conflation: demonstrated empirically (§5.4), with a structural split between method families
hypothesis_status.dss_core_hypothesis: supported on ONE attack shape only (temporally unstable colluders, §5.5: fedavg 161.3 -> 1.18). Does not catch stable colluders, by its own design.
hypothesis_status.dss_safety_as_a_wrapper: resolved 2026-08-31 (§5.11). Was the most serious problem found; wrapping a robust base could regress it up to 577x. Now cannot do materially worse than what it wraps.
hypothesis_status.dss_under_solo_attacker: OPEN. Still fails with a fragile base. Cause isolated (§5.8.1): the shared deviation reference is itself unstable when the base method is. Design problem, not arithmetic.
hypothesis_status.dss_vs_closest_prior_art: measured 2026-09-01 (section 5.14). DSS 0.64 vs FLANDERS 9.41 on adaptive_evasion; at 60% malicious DSS 0.44 vs FLANDERS 1901.7 (worse than undefended FedAvg's 1659.1). The two fail on opposite attack shapes: DSS's gate needs instability and misses stable colluders, FLANDERS rewards forecastability and prefers them.
hypothesis_status.claim_2_fairness_cost_of_the_gate: measured 2026-09-01 (section 5.15). The stability conjunct buys no fairness the collusion-only variant lacks — the shipped gate returns fedavg's numbers exactly with zero attackers, and collusion-only is already at parity. The objection blocking r2 is removed. The decision to change DSS's default remains the project owner's; thresholds are unchanged.

conclusions_overturned_by_measurement: §5.8 predicted a mechanical epsilon fix would replace the chaotic regime with a predictable one. It did not: it made results reproducible (cross-seed CV 1.03 -> 0.43) but not better, and the §5.9 joint transient window came back byte-identical. The two did not share a root cause.
§5.8's specific prescribed fix (epsilon fallback at 1e-4*n) is measurably wrong -- it fires on a unit test with clean correct discrimination and returns the sybil-dominated mean.

§5.6 concluded the AND-gate was numerically identical to stability-only. That was an artifact of its identical-Sybil attack model. Against non-identical colluders, collusion-only scores 1.09 where stability-only scores 17.13.
§5.10 found a genuine clip-radius optimum at dim=3. It does not transfer: on a 50,890-parameter model the curve is monotonic toward FedAvg with no optimum anywhere.
Section 6.5's contribution 3 ('composability with any existing Aggregator') was not novel. FLANDERS (2024) is a pre-aggregation filter over an arbitrary base. Withdrawn rather than defended.

FLANDERS's headline claim — resilience when malicious clients far exceed legitimate ones — does not hold against the adaptive attacker in our reproduction: at 60% malicious it scores 1901.7 against undefended FedAvg's 1659.1. Reported as what the numbers show; it is one attack family at dim=3 and is not a refutation of the paper's own evaluation.

Task r2's premise was wrong. It was marked 'blocked on the non-IID fairness test' for three sessions; the fairness test was not the obstacle. The harness could neither name a DSS variant nor exercise one, and nothing surfaced that because the sweep list only ever held catalog names.

The stability conjunct was assumed to be protecting Claim 2. Measured with zero attackers over 20 rounds, it protects nothing: the gate never fires, and the collusion-only variant it was guarding against is already at minority/majority parity (1.030 +/- 0.177).

Section 5.14 said FLANDERS's d-scaling was a cost 'nothing here measures'. Measuring it showed it is not a cost but a wall: quadratic in model dimension, 20.7 GB at 50,890 parameters, unrunnable without the paper's subsampling. DSS's scalar traces are constant in d. That is the sharpest distinction between the two methods and it was nearly missed.
Section 5.14's fairness note said flanders_krum 'holds' where flanders_fedavg was harmful. On a real model the paper's own Krum pairing is the harmful one: 0.102 against bare Krum's 0.655.

reproducibility.known_gap: CONFLUX_DEMO_SEED (added 2026-09-01) seeds the real-data partition but not the trainers. Residual run-to-run variance measured at 0.063 for krum; the effects being reported are ~9x larger. Synthetic experiments remain 5-seed. Real-data: section 5.16 is n=1, section 5.16.1 is n=3.
